test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A seller marks their goods 28% above the cost price. On customer demand, they offer a 25% reduction on the bills. What percentage of profit or loss does the seller make?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, a = +28% (**Mark-up**) and b = −25% (**Discount**).

Net change = 28 − 25 + (28 × (−25)) ÷ 100

Net change = 3 − (700 ÷ 100) = 3 − 7 = −4%.

Negative sign indicates a **loss** of 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mark-up = 28%, Discount = 25%.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Mark-up%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit/Loss% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/150eeba86ce6cfa778d0c925b77f5c42aa11853c38347cb96ea543463f73c17c.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 28% of 100 = 128.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 128 − 25% of 128 = 128 − (128 ÷ 4) = 128 − 32 = 96.

⇒ Since SP [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price listed by the seller, and **Discount** is always calculated on the MP to arrive at the Selling Price.

Successive Percentage Application

When a value is increased and then decreased, the result is equivalent to **successive percentage** changes: Net % = x + y + xy/100.</p
